svg.title: The guide's paddle tail: a broad flat scaly oval carried out to the wearer's right, leaning down and away on a scaly stub that leaves the body at the hip and tucks behind the leg, so the tail reads as attached rather than as a rock beside the feet. The tail is one of the two features that make a beaver identifiable at phone size, so it is drawn at full weight and never tucked behind the figure where a front-facing character would hide it. Scale is three cross bands - a rhythm, not a texture fill (art bible 1); an inner ring was tried and removed because it made the paddle read as a shell. Drawn from assets/refs/beaver/beaver-paddle-tail.jpg and beaver-ontario-full-body.jpg.
